Subject: Quick public lines for subprocessors + data transfer questions

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for taking this — procurement asked us to provide a very short, consumer-facing explanation of how Redwood uses subprocessors and what cross-border transfers look like for hosted API customers. They want copy that our legal folks can paste into the review doc and sales can paste into the console/help tooltip.

Can you share: (1) one short "tagline" ~10 words that we can show on the hosted console; (2) a 2–3 sentence public blurb for the privacy page about subprocessors and transfers; and (3) a compact 3‑bullet FAQ (plain language) that answers: "Do you use subprocessors?", "Will data leave the EU?", and "How do we find the list of subprocessors?"

We're under a tight turnaround from procurement (they want a draft by Wednesday). Attached is our checklist so you can see the exact phrasing they'd like to match.

Appreciate the help — Sam

Attachments: acme-procurement-checklist.pdf (PDF)

Hi Sam —

Thanks for the clear ask and the checklist. Quick draft below — three alternate taglines (pick one) and a short blurb + 3‑bullet FAQ. I kept the language intentionally plain for procurement/sales. Attaching a doc with the same content so your legal team can redline.

Tagline options (10 words or fewer):
- "We use trusted subprocessors to power and secure hosted inference."
- "Subprocessors help run and protect your Redwood-hosted API usage."
- "Redwood partners with vetted subprocessors for reliable, secure inference."

Public blurb (2 sentences):
Redwood uses a limited set of trusted subprocessors to operate the hosted API and provide infrastructure services (hosting, logging, analytics). We only share customer requests with subprocessors as needed to deliver the service and maintain operational security; you can view the current subprocessors list and our transfer safeguards in the DPA.

Compact FAQ (plain language):
1) Do you use subprocessors? Yes — we work with a small number of third‑party providers (for cloud hosting, content delivery, and security tooling) and vet them for security and privacy.
2) Will my data leave the EU? It depends on your configuration. Customers can choose EU-only hosting where data is kept in-region; if you use our default global hosting, requests may be processed in the region that provides the best latency and availability. We document the safeguards and transfer mechanisms in the DPA.
3) How do we find the subprocessor list? The current list is published in the DPA and linked from the console's privacy panel; we also email customers for material changes.

Next steps: Laura, Kim — could you review the phrasing for legal accuracy and DPA linkage? Sam, if this looks close to what procurement needs I can push the draft into the shared Drive so legal can redline.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Evelyn / Sam — thanks for the draft. I've reviewed and made a few edits to tighten legal alignment while keeping the copy customer-friendly. Below is an approval-ready snippet you can use in the console and a slightly expanded FAQ block for procurement. I also attached a final doc (subprocessor-public-snippets-v1.docx) with the approved lines and a suggested link target (DPA URL).

--- proposed console snippet (one line, 8–10 words):
"We partner with vetted subprocessors to operate and protect hosted API traffic."

--- short privacy blurb (publishable, 2 sentences):
Redwood engages a limited set of vetted subprocessors to run our hosted API and related services (e.g., hosting, logging, telemetry). We limit subprocessor access to what is required to provide the service, apply contractual safeguards, and publish the current subprocessor list and transfer protections in our DPA.

--- procurement-friendly 3‑bullet FAQ (approved):
• Do you use subprocessors? Yes — limited, vetted third parties support hosting, delivery, and security. They are contractually bound to our data protection requirements.
• Will data leave the EU? If you select EU-only hosting, data is kept in-region; otherwise, requests may be routed to nearby regions for performance. We rely on contractual and technical safeguards described in our DPA for cross-border transfers.
• How can I confirm who your subprocessors are? The up-to-date list is published in the DPA (link) and shown in the console privacy panel. We notify customers of significant changes and offer additional contractual safeguards upon request.

Note on DPA linkage: please point the console "Learn more" to the canonical DPA doc (https://legal.redwood.com/dpa) rather than a Google Drive copy — procurement teams expect a stable URL.

Evelyn — if you're OK with the console one-liner I'll add it to the sales snippets page and supply a small tooltip (18–25 words) for Marketing that expands on the one-line. Sam — happy to meet with your procurement folks if they want a walkthrough.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Product, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
